title: ECDO Watch
description: An interactive 3D globe and geophysical monitoring dashboard built with CesiumJS and React. Tracks real-time Kp/Dst geomagnetic indices, Earth orientation parameters (polar motion, length of day), C20 gravity coefficients, deep seismicity, and volcanic activity with animated radial pulses. Features an ancient monument alignment workbench analyzing 97 structures against a hypothesized former pole (Np'), with measured bearing axes, projected great-circle lines, signal quality heatmap overlay, and cross-channel coherence analysis across multiple time windows.
imageAlt: ECDO Watch - 3D Globe and Geophysical Dashboard

title: Thermofluidic Finance
description: A mathematical framework in which personal finance operates as a dynamical system governed by fluid mechanics and thermodynamics. Cash accounts behave as interconnected reservoirs of incompressible fluid. Volatile investments behave as compressible media subject to an exact First Law: unrealized gains are heat absorbed, realized gains are work extracted.

title: On Dynamical Systems
description: A unifying mathematical framework for dynamical systems built on the product structure Behavior = Response × Drive. Parts I–IX develop the primordial pattern, potential energy and the three energy modes (potential, kinetic, dissipative), impedance and bond-graph power conjugacy, the complete cross-domain analogy, conservation laws and constitutive relations, spectral geometry of the state manifold, and a causal underdetermination theorem showing that behavior alone cannot resolve intrinsic response from extrinsic drive without auxiliary assumptions.

title: Electrostatics Lab
description: An interactive 3D web-based visualization tool for exploring electric fields, equipotential surfaces, and field lines. Supports 11 charge configurations (point charges, dipoles, extended objects, and plate geometries). Features real-time RK4 field line integration with advanced spherical coordinate seeding, vector field glyphs, 3D equipotential surfaces via marching cubes, 2D slice views with heat maps, and a camera-aligned live cross-section. Multiple visualization modes enable students to develop spatial intuition about electromagnetic phenomena through interactive exploration.

title: SPECTRUM Market Analytics
description: Multi-dimensional market intelligence dashboard providing comprehensive asset analysis across stocks and cryptocurrencies. Features radar charts for fundamental, technical, and sentiment analysis, price history with moving averages, sector comparisons, ESG profiling, and macro factor visualization. Presents complex market signals through an intuitive dark-themed interface with tabbed navigation across analysis dimensions.

title: Eisenhower Task Manager
description: Task prioritization app using the Eisenhower Matrix framework. Track tasks across four quadrants (Do First, Schedule, Delegate, Eliminate) with completion tracking, quality ratings, and planning/execution scoring. Features both matrix and list views, recurring task support, and local data backup for personal productivity management.

title: Dynamical Systems Lab
description: An interactive React-based laboratory for exploring and visualizing dynamical systems. Includes implementations of classical systems like Lorenz attractors, pendulums, oscillators, and bifurcation phenomena. Provides real-time 3D visualization and parameter adjustment for understanding complex system behavior.

title: Two-Body Gravitational Free Fall
description: Comprehensive analysis of two equal masses falling toward each other under mutual gravitational attraction. Derives final velocities and collision times using conservation of energy, work-energy principles, and classical mechanics. Includes comparison with kinematic approximations and demonstrates the importance of accounting for variable acceleration in gravitational systems.

title: Problem-Solving and Critical Path Reasoning
description: A systematic framework for problem-solving that guides practitioners through four stages: Observation (known knowns), Analysis (known unknowns), Inference (unknown knowns), and Exploration (unknown unknowns). The PSCPR Guide Sheet provides a structured method to test claims against nulls using facts, patterns, and stories to reach evidence-based conclusions.
imageAlt: Problem-Solving and Critical Path Reasoning Thumbnail

title: Inferential Dynamics
description: This work develops a synthesis between classical logic and dynamical systems theory. The canonical inference square – Modus Ponens (MP), Modus Tollens (MT), Affirming the Consequent (AC), and Denying the Antecedent (DA) – admits a natural interpretation as a stability matrix. Valid inferences (MP, MT) act as negative-feedback eigendirections, damping error and converging toward a stable attractor: truth. Fallacies (AC, DA) operate as positive-feedback eigendirections, amplifying error and driving divergence. The symmetry parallels James Clerk Maxwell's On Governors (1868), where perturbations may diminish, grow, or oscillate with increasing or decreasing amplitude depending on feedback sign and eigenvalue placement. Framed this way, Aristotle's concern with valid inference, Maxwell's concern with mechanical stability, and the modern eigenvalue criterion of dynamical systems are recognized as structurally isomorphic descriptions of reality.

title: Rebound Pendulum
description: The rebound pendulum explores how energy is lost during impact. By connecting rebound height, velocity, and angular deflection to the coefficient of restitution, this project reveals how a simple device can yield deep insights into material response and collision efficiency. It bridges theory and measurement, offering experimental methods for quantifying energy loss in a system traditionally used to model ideal motion.

title: Certainty, Inference, and Comprehension
description: Critical thinking is a term widely used in academics yet is a weak form of logical inference akin to abduction, and especially weak as compared to induction or a stronger form of inference - deduction. By establishing a framework which prioritizes questions over answers and function over form, and by investigating modes of inferential logic, reexamining the scientific method, and distinguishing between comprehension and understanding, a deductive "critical path" of logical inference is prescribed to effectively prosecute hypotheses and disrupt paradigm.

title: Horizontal Frame Centering Algorithm
description: A practical mathematical solution for evenly spacing picture frames on a wall. Derives equations to determine optimal frame placement such that gaps between frame edges and wall edges are uniform, with analytical formulas for calculating frame center positions given wall width, frame width, and frame count.

title: Universe of Proportions
description: A conceptual exploration of ratios and proportions as the universal language underlying physics, engineering, biology, chemistry, and mathematics. From Babylonian clay tablets to modern physics, the work demonstrates how analogical thinking through proportions reveals deep structural patterns. Central claim: anything dimensionally equivalent can be expressed as a ratio—and discovering meaningful proportionalities across domains is the essence of scientific understanding. Explores applications from Kepler's laws to genetic ratios, spring constants to photosynthesis, Archimedes' principle to the golden ratio.

title: Fundamental Principles - On Analogies (continued)
description: Continuation of physical analogies framework, extending the source-field-force model across diverse domains. Explores how fundamental mathematical structures reveal isomorphic patterns in mechanics, electromagnetism, thermodynamics, and abstract systems, demonstrating the power of analogical reasoning in physics and philosophy.

title: On Physical Analogies
description: Foundational exploration of structural analogies between physical systems, introducing the unifying concept of sources interacting with fields to produce forces. Examines how this framework applies across mechanics, electrostatics, and thermodynamics, revealing deep connections between seemingly distinct phenomena.

title: Gravitational Radiation
description: A Masters thesis extending Oliver Heaviside's 1893 analogy between gravitation and electromagnetism. By deriving gravitational field equations, retarded potentials, and radiation patterns using Maxwell-Heaviside formalism, this work models how accelerated masses emit gravitational radiation analogously to electric dipole radiation. Notably, the formulation predicts a reversal in the Poynting vector, implying gravitational fields gain energy rather than lose it—a paradox that challenges our understanding of gravitational energy flow and the speed of gravitational propagation.

title: Disk Cam Synthesis
description: A custom cam design and optimization tool developed in Visual Basic for Applications that democratizes mechanical engineering design. Users input desired motion profiles and the system calculates the required cam geometry, kinematic derivatives (position, velocity, acceleration, jerk), animated simulations, and exportable CAD files. Most innovatively, the tool generates 3D-printer-ready G-code directly—enabling rapid prototyping and manufacturing of custom cams. Designed as an affordable, educational alternative to expensive commercial software, it bridges theory, simulation, and physical manufacturing.

title: Nonlinear Human Population Growth Modeling
description: A collaborative research project deriving nonlinear growth models from chemical kinetics theory and fitting them to nearly 2,000 years of historical population data. Using Excel's Solver to optimize parameters, we compared multiple model forms (exponential, logistic, power-law) across different data windows. Results demonstrate that while models agree on historical data, their long-term forecasts diverge dramatically—some predicting exponential growth, others stabilization or collapse. The work illustrates how mathematical modeling can bound plausible futures while revealing the sensitivity of predictions to model structure and parameter values.

title: Gravitational Wave Detector
description: Zener Diode Quantum Detector for Gravitational Wave Research – This senior design project built and tested a low-cost tabletop apparatus based on R.T. Cahill's theoretical framework for detecting quantum fluctuations in reverse-biased Zener diodes. The team constructed the measurement system with high-resolution analog-to-digital conversion and developed a data analysis pipeline for processing and filtering collected measurements. The apparatus was systematically tested for sensitivity to environmental factors including temperature, microwaves, humidity, and vibrations. Testing revealed that temperature affected readings as expected for Zener diodes, while microwave and humidity tests showed no significant effects. The project created design specifications and test procedures for future research, explicitly noting that gravitational wave detection analysis was beyond the project scope. While no conclusive evidence of gravitational wave detection was found, the work provides a foundation for continued investigation into quantum detector sensitivity.
